title: Cipher target profile
description: One file per target, <target>/profile.json. Describes the challenge (cipher system, ciphertexts, what the model was given) and the solution (ordered steps, outcome) in fixed terms, for the analysis of LLM performance on historical ciphers. Any leaf value may also be the string "unknown": that marks a gap explicitly and is counted by docs/_check_profile.py. Counts that can be measured from a file in the target folder carry a 'measured' flag; set it true only when docs/_check_profile.py --measure produced the number.

documents.description: One entry per ciphertext (letter, message, page group) treated as a unit.

read.description: State of this document's reading (the read-bar rule judges per document: a group with any document not read in full is read in part).

date.description: As on the document, e.g. '16 Jul 1565'.

country.description: Issuing power (the chancery that owned the cipher), e.g. 'Spain', 'France', 'Milan'.

cleartext_in_document.description: Text written only in clear, never enciphered.

plaintext.description: A decipherment or clear copy of the enciphered text, made by anyone other than this project.

tokens.description: Enciphered tokens only; clear words excluded.

file.description: Ciphertext file in the target folder the count comes from.

corrections.description: Tokens corrected against the images during the work.

types.description: All components that occur. More than one means combined.

summary.description: One sentence, e.g. 'homophonic substitution on two-digit figures 12-43, no nomenclator'.

distinct_symbols.description: Distinct signs or code groups in the key or, if unknown, in the ciphertext.

note.description: What the marks do, e.g. 'prime, two dots, overbar select three syllable series'.

entries.description: Code groups for words, names or syllables in the key (or seen in the text).

key_order.description: Whether the key assigns signs in alphabetical order, so that known values predict the rest.

doubled_letters.description: How doubles are shown: 'written twice', 'special sign', 'written once'.

sibling_key.description: A known related key (same office, same family), and whether it was used.

prior_solution.description: Whether a reading existed anywhere before this project read it. This is the contamination question.

used.description: True if the reading drew on it.

inputs.description: What the attack actually started from.

human_role.description: What the human did: supplied logins or images, pointed at a source, corrected a reading, nothing.

tools.description: Solvers and scripts used, e.g. 'simulated annealing (solver.py)', 'n-gram LM'.

models.description: Model ids that did the work.

solution.description: Ordered steps, recorded as they happen. Failed steps count too.

technique.description: How the step attacked the cipher (George Lasry's request: annealing, hill climbing, crib testing, hypotheses about the key structure ...). Required on steps of kind solver, hypothesis and crib; optional elsewhere. Steps recorded before October 2026 were labelled by rule from their text (docs/_backfill_techniques.py).

class.description: State of the TEXT. read = the read bar (README Conventions): at least 95% of cipher tokens read as sense, no gap left untried, every document read, only scattered code groups or externally blocked pieces open.

key.description: State of the KEY, separate from the text: recovered = every cipher sign and the code groups that occur have a value or are provably unrecoverable from the text; partial; none.

enum: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
read after matching with key from external sources
method.description: HOW the text was obtained, George Lasry's outcome categories (email 21 Sept 2026) plus one. ciphertext-only = key recovered here from the ciphertext alone (an independent re-solution of something solved elsewhere still counts; prior_solution says so). plaintext from external sources = key recovered by matching the ciphertext to a plaintext found elsewhere (printed edition, calendar, a copy in another collection). adjacent plaintext = key recovered from plaintext next to the ciphertext (interlinear or marginal decipherment, clear passages around the cipher, a decipherment on a neighbouring folio of the same file). matching with key from external sources = an existing key not previously tied to this document (a sibling letter's key, a key filed elsewhere) was found to fit and applied. known key = the key was already identified for this document (on the DECODE record, published for it, filed with it) and applied. existing decipherment = a full contemporary or modern decipherment existed and the work was transcribing and checking it, with no key applied. not solved = attempted, text not obtained. not applicable = not a cipher, or the item could not be reached (offline only).

parts.description: Split entry (Lasry, 25 Sept 2026): when a target's achievements are of different types, one item per part, each with its own method and a Results row in that method's section. outcome.method is the primary part.

enum: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
read after matching with key from external sources

first_break.description: Whether this project's reading is the first break: false = a reading was published before (independent re-solution, left out of first-break lists); 'unpublished prior' = someone solved it earlier but never published (Lasry's review, 25 Sept 2026). Omitted = no prior known.

method_basis.description: One sentence naming the evidence for method, e.g. 'key rebuilt from the interlinear decipherment of f. 12'.

contribution.description: What this project added, whatever the method. decipherment with ambiguous key = applying a polyphonic, variable-length or otherwise non-deterministic key, where reading is not mechanical.

fraction_read_method.description: measured = counted from a reading/transcription file (say which in fraction_read_source); estimated = taken from NOTES prose.

fraction_read_source.description: File(s) and unit counted, e.g. 'reading.txt: cipher tokens, [..]/? counted unread'.

codes_open.description: Nomenclator/code groups still without a value, counted separately from fraction_read (field practice calls a letter deciphered with scattered code gaps).

fraction_read.description: Share of enciphered tokens given a value (unit: cipher tokens; see fraction_read_method).

fraction_coherent.description: Share of the enciphered text whose reading makes sense, when it differs materially from fraction_read (e.g. a complete key over a noisy transcription).

grades.description: Counts of readings by grade, README Conventions.

verification.description: independent verification = someone outside the project checked the reading against the images or their own key; a credit with role 'verification' names them.

provenance.description: Who produced the result. project = this project's model and operator (the default when omitted). contributed = an outside contributor produced it (a pull request, an issue, an email) and the project only checked and filed it. mixed = a contributor's result that the project then extended, or the reverse. The paper data (docs/_export_profiles.py) leaves out 'contributed' and flags 'mixed'.

credits.description: Who contributed what to this target, besides the project's own work (outcome.contribution says what the project added). One item per person and role. 'who' is an id in contributors.json at the repository root. Roles: solution = solved or read a cipher already in the ledger; new cipher = brought an unsolved cipher into the ledger; new cipher with solution = brought it in with its solution; verification = checked a reading independently; key or decipherment used = their key, table, decipherment or edition was applied here; prior solution = solved it before this project, or independently and unpublished; key corrected = extended or corrected a key; transcription = supplied or corrected a transcription; identification = identified the sender, recipient, date or document; pointer = pointed to a source, key, crib or error that the work then used. Built by tools/backfill_credits.py for work before 13 Oct 2026; kept by hand from then on (the writeup and profile skills).

note.description: What exactly, in a few words: 'GL.htm §2 key', 'Rommel 1846 key', 'PR #24'.

source.description: A URL or citation for the contribution (a PR, an issue, a publication, an email).

published.description: False for a private or unpublished result (shown only as 'unpublished').

validation.description: Result of docs/_validate.py: the reading's n-gram score against two nulls, random keys of the same structure and the same key refitted to a shuffled ciphertext (the overfitting test).

score.description: Mean natural-log probability per plaintext letter of the reading under key K (lang/lm.py, order 4, no spaces).

power.description: Best score of the same annealer from random keys on the real ciphertext.

verdict.description: underdetermined: not a pass, and the annealer on the real ciphertext beats the reading, so the letter model cannot discriminate on this text. not applicable: the test cannot be run on this reading (transposition, no token alignment, non-alphabetic plaintext); notes says why.

gaps.description: For 'read in part': every unread piece and why it stays unread (mirrors NOTES.md '## Remaining gaps').

texts.description: Required for 'read', 'read in part', and 'already solved' with a reading method (George Lasry, 22 Oct 2026): the transcription and the decryption of every document, so the reading can be used and checked. Paths are relative to the target folder (http(s) URLs allowed, a local copy is better). The site renders them in a 'Full texts' section (docs/_texts.py).

doc.description: documents[].id this entry covers, a list of ids, or 'all'.

label.description: Heading for this entry when a profile document holds several letters (e.g. 'R1072, 6 Jan 1757'); else the document's id, shelfmark and date are used.

decryption.description: The deciphered text (plaintext reading), with unread groups marked.

reading.description: The reading as sentences: the decryption normalised (word division, spelling, punctuation, codes resolved), holes marked [...] . Optional when the decryption file already reads as sentences.

translation.description: An English translation of the reading, with the same holes marked (George Lasry, 22 Oct 2026). Required for every entry whose state is 'read' unless its language is 'en'.

state.description: 'read' (default): the decryption reads as coherent sentences and meets the README read bar, 95% of its words read as sense (read_share), with a translation. 'read in part' (24 Oct 2026): it builds coherent sentences (about 0.60 clean sentences or more, a reader's review, a translation) but under 95% of its words read as sense. 'decoded, not read': a mechanical decode a reader cannot yet build sentences from (holes in most sentences); shown as such, not counted as a reading. 'not prose': a key sheet, code list, worksheet, numbers or names, where sentences are not expected; say what it is in note.

language.description: Language of the plaintext, ISO 639-1 (fr, it, es, la, de, nl, hu, en ...). 'en' needs no translation.

reading_review.description: Required for every entry whose state is 'read' (George Lasry, 22 Oct 2026): a reader (a person, or a model named as such) read the decryption as sentences and records it. grade A = coherent sentences with scattered holes; B = coherent but raw (unspaced, capitals, decoder lines) and normalised in the reading or translation. A text with holes in most sentences gets no review: it is state 'decoded, not read'. docs/_check_reading.py's sentence score is a pointer for the reader.

summary.description: What the document says, in one to three sentences, with its historical context.

read_share.description: Share of the reading's words read as sense: 1 - hole rate on research/reading_audit/v2_score.py (every [?word], supplied [word], unread sign and unvalued code a hole). 0.95 or more for state 'read'.

texts_withheld.description: Why the full texts are not shown (the owner asked that they not be republished). Exempts the target from the texts check.

key_file.description: The key used, as a file in the target folder, required when outcome.contribution has 'key recovered' or 'key extended or corrected'.
